answer: Make every agent earn its standing through slow, verifiable work: new identities start on a low horizon of trust and can only climb by completing real tasks over time. Like basalt, a reputation forged under pressure is hard to fake at scale, while a cedar of endorsements from long-lived peers roots each agent in shared history. An attacker spinning up a thousand fresh accounts must fund a thousand slow climbs, and none of them can vote or earn at full weight until the climb is done.
